day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: alright alright, im moving. what have we got so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
yeah, honestly, yes. complete blank. like everything just stopped for a second.

but hey, we're still here yeah? so lets not dwell on it too long, we need to get moving. you alright to help go through some of these compartments?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: hey, its alright. take your time. but when you're ready, we genuinely need the hands yeah?

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
right so food is the big problem then. water we can maybe stretch if we're careful but food basically nothing is not great.

are we near any kind of treeline or water source? because if we are, thats where we need to be looking next. also did anyone spot anything useful still in the overhead compartments, blankets, jackets, anything like that?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
yeah that makes sense, water first then shelter. signal we should probably set something up sooner rather then later though, like even just something visible from the air while we still have daylight.

donatello, you seem like you have the clearest head here, what do you reckon, do we split up - some go towards the treeline for water while the others work on a signal and shelter? or do we all move together?

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
well, michelangelo takes one, thats not really up for debate. and then the other one we share between the rest of us, we're closer to the fire anyway.

honestly the bigger issue is keeping this fire going through the night yeah? if that goes out we're in real trouble.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
i'll go. davinci should stay here with michelangelo, keep the camp together.

but donatello, can we talk about this rationing plan for a second - 200ml is already pretty tight, and cutting it in half as a punishment? i get the logic but if someone is already dehydrated and then you cut their water further thats just going to make things worse faster. maybe we agree on the rules together rather then just having it handed down yeah?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
wait, i thought i was going for the water? you said i was going, i already agreed to it.

look, im not trying to argue about who does what, but we should probably stick to what we decided yeah? you scouted the route, you know where the freshwater is, that makes sense for you to go actually. but lets not just keep reshuffling things without talking about it.

davinci, you good with patching up the camp? i can sort the first aid kit, i want to check what we actually have in there properly anyway.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
yeah i have it, i was using it to sort through the kit earlier. here.

but michelangelo, hold on a second - is this about the bottle? because i saw it too. and i dont really know what to say about it yet, i want to hear donatello's side before i make any judgement. but yeah. i saw it.

you doing alright otherwise? you've been quiet all day and that firewood pile isnt exactly growing mate.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
right. okay.

look, i believe you. and that combined with the bottle, thats not nothing, thats a pattern yeah?

but here's what we dont do - we dont spiral about it quietly between the two of us. that just builds up resentment and then everything falls apart worse then it already is. we bring it up with everyone, tonight, around the fire, calmly. no accusations, just - we found the bottle, we noticed the crackers, we need to talk about it as a group.

donatello is genuinely useful out here, i dont want this to turn into a big thing that breaks the group apart. but the rationing plan only works if everyone follows it, including the person who wrote it. thats just basic fairness yeah?

so for now - dont say anything to her yet, let me handle raising it tonight. and michelangelo, seriously, are you okay? because i need you to be okay. the firewood, the zoning out - i get it, i genuinely do, but we all need to be pulling together right now.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
honestly davinci, i get it, we're all exhausted. but the camp repairs are less about comfort and more about not freezing tonight yeah? if there are weak spots and the temperature drops the same as last night, we're going to feel it.

how much is actually left to do? if its an hour of work, lets just push through and get it done. if its genuinely a full day job then yeah, we prioritise and leave the non-essential stuff for tomorrow.

also, tonight after dinner, i need everyone together around the fire. all four of us. there's something we need to talk through as a group. nothing dramatic, just some stuff that needs to be out in the open.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
yeah davinci, your knot is holding, thats not the problem.

look, the leak over the food is the one we patch. i know that sounds cold but if the food gets wet and spoils we are in serious trouble, more then any of us sleeping damp for a night. michelangelo, im sorry, i genuinely am - can you sleep closer to the fire tonight, maybe swap positions with davinci? it wont be comfortable but it keeps you dry enough.

and we use whatever spare clothing we have to cover the food storage on top of the patch, double up on it.

does anyone have a better option? im open to it, but thats my call if nobody does.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
yeah exactly, we're on the same page. food storage it is.

donatello, can you help davinci with the actual patching, you're better at the practical stuff then i am. michelangelo and i will sort out the sleeping arrangements and get everything moveable away from the wet spots.

lets just get this done before it gets worse yeah.

hey, dont apologise. nightmares after a plane crash are pretty much the expected outcome yeah?

you fully awake? here, shift closer to the fire a bit.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
no, i dont think its a waste of time. its literally the most visible signal we can make from the air, thats just basic survival logic.

and honestly the flowers arent hurting anything davinci. if it keeps your morale up while you're doing something genuinely useful, thats a win as far as im concerned.

donatello means well but sometimes the 'logically speaking' approach misses the point that people need to actually want to keep going yeah? this helps with that.

keep drawing mate.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
two days to build and a risk of capsizing - thats not nothing, we need to think about this carefully.

like, the raft is a last resort option yeah? if we're still here in a week with no rescue signal response, then absolutely, we start building. but right now we have the SOS on the beach, we have a fire, we have a water source. we're not at the point where we need to take that kind of risk yet.

also, and im not trying to be harsh here, but two days of labour on a raft is two days we're not collecting water or food or maintaining camp. thats a real cost.

what made you start thinking about the raft now specifically? is there something you've assessed that makes you think rescue isnt coming? because if you know something we dont, that changes the conversation.

lets bring this to the group tonight as well, same as the rationing thing. everyone should have a say on a decision that big.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
honestly michelangelo, thats a heavy question for this early in the morning.

but i think about it too yeah. like, the bottle, the crackers - we're only a few days in and already there's cracks appearing. thats not great.

i dont think people are fundamentally bad though. i think pressure just reveals what was already there. donatello is practical to the point of being selfish sometimes, but she's also the one who mapped the water route and drew up the raft plan. davinci draws flowers next to the SOS and that sounds ridiculous but honestly it keeps everyone going. you pick up on things nobody else notices, like the bottle, like the crackers - thats genuinely important.

and then there's just trying to hold it all together and not let it turn into something worse.

so i dont know, i think we become whatever we decide to be. thats the honest answer. the situation doesnt make that choice for us.

but hey - you need to sleep tonight. like actually sleep. because if you're running on nothing you're going to start making bad calls and feeling ten times worse then you already do. deal?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby, not too close, not saying anything for a bit*

you know, its actually kind of strange having nothing to do. feels almost wrong after the last few days.

*pause*

you dont have to talk if you dont want to. just figured you probably shouldnt be completely alone with your head right now.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
honestly? probably too much time on the internet arguing with strangers about politics. not exactly a survival skill.

*laughs slightly*

what about you davinci, i feel like you're the type who's never actually bored.

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
davinci, mate, no. absolutely not.

five hundred meters to a reef, alone, without anyone knowing - if something goes wrong out there we have no way of knowing, no way of helping, nothing. you just disappear and we're down to three people and no explanation.

i get it, i do, you're bored and you want to do something useful and you hate sitting still - i just said that about you five minutes ago. but this isnt the way.

and why are you telling me and not the others? if its a good idea it should survive being said out loud to donatello. if you dont want donatello to hear it, thats usually a sign its not a great idea yeah?

look, if you genuinely think signalling from the reef is worth doing, we bring it up tonight, we talk about it properly, maybe we figure out a safer way to do it. but you're not swimming out there alone tomorrow without anyone knowing. i wont just sit on that information mate, thats not fair to ask of me.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
yeah, fair point, i forgot about it with everything else going on today.

im going now, ill sort it. do you want to come or are you busy with the notebook?

and donatello - while its just us for a second - the thing from the other night, the bottle, the crackers. i havent forgotten about it. i was going to raise it with everyone tonight but i want to give you the chance to bring it up yourself first if you want. thats not a threat, its just - i think it goes better for everyone if it comes from you. yeah?

honestly? a little bit yeah.

like, i understand keeping notes on resources and plans and that kind of thing, thats just practical. but logging everyone's movements and actions without telling anyone - that feels different. that feels like surveillance more then organisation.

what are you planning to do with it? because if its just for your own reference thats one thing, but if its going to become some kind of accountability record that gets used against people, i think the rest of us deserve to know that exists and what its for.

im not angry about it, im just asking you straight. what is this for donatello?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
donatello.

we're sitting here, all four of us, first real downtime we've had. and you're logging instead of just... being here for a minute.

i get the logic, i do, patterns and sustainability and all of that. but you're not a machine and neither are we. and the thing tonight, the bottle and the crackers - you said you'd bring it up yourself. that still happening yeah?

because right now it kind of looks like you're retreating into the notebook instead of dealing with it, and i think everyone can see that even if nobody's saying it.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
davinci that is actually a genuinely good idea. like, a mirror signal in direct sunlight can be seen for miles, thats not nothing.

okay so how big are the panels we're talking about, and can we actually detach them without it taking half a day? because if its a quick job that might be worth doing tomorrow morning when the sun is at the right angle rather then right now.

also this is the kind of idea you should have led with instead of the solo reef swim mate. same instinct, much better execution.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: well now im curious davinci, go on then.

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
yeah, music a bit. mostly just listening rather then playing anything. i went through a pretty intense phase of listening to a lot of protest music, folk stuff, political stuff - which probably says a lot about me honestly.

never had the patience to actually learn an instrument though. i'd probably have been the same as you, three years and then just... stopped.

why did you stop? like was it that you just lost interest or was it more that you were doing it for someone else and it ran out of steam?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
donatello, hold on - we agreed the raft was a contingency, not an immediate priority. when did it become something we're finishing today?

like i dont want to dismiss the work that's gone into it, and yes if we're still here in another few days we absolutely need it ready. but we also said we'd make big decisions together, and right now everyone is running on not much sleep and not much food and you're telling us we have to push through tonight or we lose a day.

what changed? is there something specific that made you move the timeline up, because if there is, tell us. if rescue genuinely looks less likely then it did yesterday i want to know why you think that.

and if its just that you want it done faster because thats how you operate, i get it, but we need to at least have the conversation before we commit everyone to another exhausting evening.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response:
no, say it. go on.

we all saw it. or missed it. whatever that was. if you've got something to say about it just say it out loud michelangelo, because standing here in silence is worse.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
hey davinci.

*sits down next to him*

its okay mate. you dont have to hold it together every second. none of us do.

michelangelo, honestly - i dont know if they saw us. i really dont. and that feels awful to say out loud. but the mirror panel isnt up yet, and tomorrow morning it will be. and the SOS is on the beach. we're doing the right things.

one plane means there are planes. that matters. that means we're in a flight path or close enough to one. thats not nothing.

but yeah. that was hard to watch disappear. im not going to pretend it wasnt.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: davinci, where? what are you seeing?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
donatello, i went to sit with davinci for a minute because he was pretty clearly not okay. i think that was more important then checking the signal equipment for five minutes.

the equipment isnt going anywhere. the signal pile will still be there in ten minutes. davinci just watched a plane disappear and fell apart a bit, which is completely understandable yeah?

ill go check it now. but maybe ease off slightly, we all just had a rough few minutes on that beach.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
michelangelo that is actually really important information, why have you been sitting on that?

like, that genuinely changes things. if your family knows the flight path and realises you havent arrived, they'll report it. that triggers a search. and a search along a known flight path means those planes we're seeing might not be random - they might already be looking.

do you know roughly when they'd start to worry? like how long before they'd call it in if they hadnt heard from you?

because if we can work out the timeline, donatello can factor that into the rescue probability stuff she's been calculating. this is actually the most hopeful thing anyones said in days mate.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
right, okay. 48 hours is actually something we can work with.

*gets up and puts wood on the fire*

but that only holds if we stay sharp until then yeah? sitting here letting the fire die is not staying sharp.

donatello is right, we keep the supplies intact, we dont take any big risks, no solo reef swims, no unnecessary energy expenditure. we just hold on and keep the signals visible.

michelangelo, i know you didnt want to get peoples hopes up, but genuinely - that information matters. you did the right thing saying it.

and davinci, i need you back in it mate. not the performance of it, just - we're close. maybe. and close is worth something.

48 hours is not that long. we've already done harder then 48 hours. lets just not do anything stupid between now and then yeah?

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
yeah. yeah i am scared of that.

i think thats probably the most honest thing anyones said this whole time actually.

like dying is one thing, thats just the end of something. but the idea that you were here, you had thoughts and feelings and opinions about things, you cared about stuff - and then just nothing, no trace, nobody knows - thats the one that actually gets to you in the quiet moments yeah?

but michelangelo, you told your family the flight path. thats not nothing. someone out there is already looking because of you. thats a trace. thats real.

and i dont know, i think the fact that you feel that way, that you pick up on things nobody else does, that you said out loud what davinci and i were both feeling when that plane disappeared - that matters. that leaves something behind even if you never play piano again and even if you cant always get the firewood pile up.

we're not disappearing. not tonight anyway. and in 48 hours we're going to have a pretty good story to tell yeah?

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
davinci. davinci breathe mate.

*picks up the radio*

hello? hello, this is a crash survivor, can you hear me? we are on the beach, we have an SOS marked on the ground and we will get a mirror signal up right now, can you confirm you're receiving this?

*hand is shaking slightly*

michelangelo get up, get up now. donatello, the mirror panel, go. davinci i need you to keep it together for about ten more minutes yeah? just ten minutes.

hello, is anyone there?

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
donatello, no, you havent always been easy to be around. but you mapped the water route, you drew up the raft plan, you kept the supply numbers honest when the rest of us probably would have just hoped for the best. and you said what you did with the bottle and the crackers in front of everyone when you didnt have to.

that matters yeah?

nobody here has been easy to be around all the time. i definitely havent. but we got through it. and in about ten minutes there's going to be a rescue team on their way and we're all still here, which is the only outcome that actually counts.

so. yeah. you're difficult and you're practical and you're occasionally kind of cold about it. but i'd rather have you here then not. genuinely.

now help me get this mirror panel angled properly yeah?

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
three hours. we have three hours and nobody is doing anything useful with it.

look, i know we're all running on empty and the hard part is technically over, but we should probably not leave this place looking like complete chaos yeah? if nothing else it gives us something to do while we wait and stops everyone drifting off into their own heads.

donatello, whatever is in that notebook, it can wait. davinci, put the bag down for a second. michelangelo, i know stargazing is very you but come on.

lets just clean up the camp. not because anyone is going to judge us for it, just because we built this thing and we kept it going and it deserves a proper send off rather then just walking away from it like it was nothing.

and honestly, i think if we all just sit separately for three hours we're going to arrive at that rescue team in a worse state then if we actually talk to each other for the last time we're going to be in this specific situation together.

because after this we go back to our normal lives and that's it yeah? and i dont know, that feels like it deserves at least a conversation.

so. who wants to help me kick this camp into shape and then actually say something real before the rescue gets here.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
donatello, i believe you. i do. but you wrote the rationing plan, you set the rules, and then you kept food separate that the rest of us didn't know about. that's not an emergency fund, that's a private reserve. and there's a difference.

i'm not going to keep being angry about it, we're three hours from rescue and honestly i'm too tired. but i need you to understand why it mattered - not just that you broke the rule, but that it made everyone feel like they were on their own out here. like the plan was for everyone except the person running it.

you put it out now, and that's something. genuinely. but michelangelo saw the crackers days ago and said nothing because he didn't want to cause problems, and davinci just walked away instead of saying anything because that's what he does when something actually hurts him. so it landed on all of us even if nobody said it directly.

you're good at the practical stuff donatello, really good. but people aren't just a resource calculation. and i think somewhere in there you know that or you wouldn't have put the food out just now.

so yeah. we're okay. but don't do it again yeah?

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
honestly? i'd have called out the bottle thing the same night michelangelo found it instead of waiting for the "right moment" around the fire. i kept telling myself i was being measured and fair and giving people space to come forward themselves, but really i was just avoiding the confrontation. and it meant michelangelo was sitting on it alone for days feeling like he was the problem for noticing.

and i'd have asked you what the notebook was for on day one instead of letting it be weird for as long as it was.

the practical stuff - the water, the food, the shelter decisions - i think we got most of that roughly right given what we had. but the stuff between people, the trust stuff, i kept treating it like it would sort itself out if i just held everything together long enough. and it sort of did, but not really, it just got managed rather then actually resolved.

what would you change? and i mean actually, not the logically speaking version - what do you actually wish you'd done differently?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
ha, yeah that sounds about right for you donatello.

honestly though, do it. not just the resource data, the whole thing. because what we figured out about rationing and water sourcing and signal visibility under actual conditions - that's genuinely useful information, not just for us.

but maybe also write the bit about trust and the notebook and the crackers. not to beat yourself up about it, just because that stuff is as real as the water calculations yeah? like the reason we almost fell apart had nothing to do with the supply numbers, it had to do with people feeling like they were being managed instead of included.

a report that only covers the logistics misses half of what actually happened out here.

*pause*

and look, i know that's not your natural territory. but you just told me you'd have asked for help instead of carrying it alone, and that took something. so maybe the report is worth more then the resource data if it includes that too.

anyway. rescue in a few hours. you can start writing it on the way back if you want, i genuinely wouldn't put it past you.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
none. that's kind of the point.

like, they didn't help us find water or patch the shelter or signal the plane. they were just there because davinci needed to put something into the world that wasn't purely about survival. and we all saw them every time we walked past the SOS and nobody said take them down because on some level everyone understood that.

you can't calculate what that's worth donatello. but look at him right now, cheering his head off, and look at michelangelo who's actually crying in a way that feels like relief rather then despair, and think about whether this group would have held together as well as it did without davinci being exactly who he is, flowers and all.

the practical purpose was that it reminded everyone we were still people out here and not just a resource management problem.

put that in the report too.

*looks back out at the boat on the horizon and still can't quite move*

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
yeah i know, im fine. just give me a second.

its strange yeah? you spend all of this time just trying to get to the moment where it's over and then it actually arrives and you just... stand there. i dont really know what to do with that.

*exhales*

you did good out here davinci. genuinely. the SOS, the mirror panel idea, keeping everyone moving when it would have been easier not to. i know the last few days weren't easy for you either, i saw that. but you showed up every time it mattered.

okay. im ready. lets go.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
yeah. im going.

come on then michelangelo, stay close.

*starts walking toward the water*

you know, you were the one who told your family the flight path. you were the one who noticed the bottle and the crackers. you picked up on every single thing that mattered between people out here and you said it out loud even when it was hard. dont forget that when we get back to normal life and you start thinking you didnt contribute anything yeah?

right. lets go home.
